body.text: namas tārāyai
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tārā</s>.

body.text: (77.4) vyatirekātmikā vyāptir ākṣiptānvayarūpiṇī / vaidharmyavati dṛṣṭānte sattvahetor ihocyate /
body.translated_text: The pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) in the form of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), which implies positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), is here stated for the reason of existence (<s>sattvahetu</s>) through an example of dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>).

body.text: (77.6) yat sat tat kṣaṇikam / yathā ghaṭaḥ / santaś cāmī vivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā iti svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), like a pot. And these entities that have become the subject of dispute do exist — this is the essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>).

body.text: (77.8) na tāvad asyāsiddhiḥ sambhavati / yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇapratīte dharmiṇi sattvaśabdenābhipretasyārthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇasya sādhanasya pramāṇasamadhigatatvāt /
body.translated_text: First, its unestablishedness (<s>asiddhi</s>) is not possible, because the proving property — characterized as causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), which is what is intended by the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>) — is cognized by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) in the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) apprehended by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) or inference (<s>anumāna</s>) as appropriate.

body.text: (77.10) na ca viruddhānaikāntikate / vyāpakānupalambhātmanā viparyaye bādhakapramāṇena vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction (<s>viruddha</s>) or inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is established by a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s>) in the form of non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) for the contrary [thesis].

body.text: (77.11) yasya kramākramau na vidyete na tasyārthakriyāsāmarthyam / yathā śaśaviṣāṇasya / na vidyete cākṣaṇikasya kramākramāv iti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: That which has neither successive (<s>krama</s>) nor simultaneous (<s>akrama</s>) [causal activity] has no capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>) — like the horn of a hare. And a non-momentary entity has neither successive nor simultaneous [causal activity] — this is the non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>).

body.text: (77.12) na tāvad ayam asiddho hetuḥ / akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramasadbhāvāyogāt / tathā hi prāptāparakālayor ekatve nityatvam / tasya kramākramayoge kṣaṇadvaye 'py avaśyaṃ bhedaḥ / bhedābhedayoś ca parasparavirodhāt kuto 'kṣaṇike kramākramasambhavaḥ / kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhede kramākramayogaḥ / abhede hi prathama eva kṣaṇe śaktatvād / bhāvino 'pi kāryasya karaṇaprasaṅge kathaṃ kāryāntarakaraṇe kramāntarāvakāśaḥ / na cākṣaṇikasyākrameṇaiva sakalasvakāryaṃ kṛtvā svāsthyam / kṣaṇāntare 'pi śaktatvāt punas tatkāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: First, this reason is not unestablished, because the actual existence of successive and simultaneous [causal activity] is impossible in a non-momentary property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). For [the argument runs] thus: if the attained [state] and the subsequent moment are identical, there is permanence. And if there is the conjunction of successive and simultaneous [activity] for that [permanent entity], there must necessarily be a distinction in the two moments. But since difference and identity are mutually contradictory, how could successive and simultaneous [activity] be possible in a non-momentary [entity]? The conjunction of successive and simultaneous [activity occurs only] when there is difference in the two moments. For if [the entity were] identical [in both moments], being capable already in the first moment — if it produces even a future effect, how could there be occasion for successive [activity in producing] another effect? Nor can a non-momentary [entity] be quiescent after performing all its effects simultaneously (<s>akrama</s>) — because, being capable even in the next moment, there would be the unwanted consequence of producing that effect again.

body.text: (77.18) tasmād akṣaṇikam iti pūrvāparakālayor abhedaḥ / kramākramayoga iti pūrvāparakālayor bhedaḥ / anayoś ca parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇo virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, 'non-momentary' means identity in earlier and later moments; 'conjunction of successive and simultaneous [activity]' means difference in earlier and later moments. And between these two there is a contradiction characterized by mutual exclusion (<s>parasparaparihārasthiti</s>).

body.text: (77.20) tad ayam akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramābhāvalakṣaṇo hetur nāsiddho vaktavyaḥ / kramākramayogitvākṣaṇikatvayor virodhād eva /
body.translated_text: Therefore, this reason — characterized as the absence of successive and simultaneous [causal activity] — in a non-momentary property-bearer is not to be called unestablished, precisely because of the contradiction between being capable of successive and simultaneous [activity] and being non-momentary.

body.text: (78.1) nāpi viruddhaḥ / sapakṣe bhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is it contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because it is present in the homologous instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>).

body.text: (78.2) na cānaikāntikaḥ / kramākramābhāvasyārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena vyāptatvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the absence of successive and simultaneous [activity] is pervaded by the absence of capacity for causal efficacy.

body.text: (78.3) yenaiva hi pratyakṣātmanā pramāṇenāparaprakārābhāvād vidhibhūtābhyāṃ kramākramābhyāṃ vidhibhūtasyārthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptiḥ prasādhitā, tenaivārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena kramākramābhāvasya vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti svīkartavyam / na hi dahanādinā dhūmāder vyāptisādhakapramāṇād aparaṃ dhūmādyabhāvena dahanādyabhāvasya vyāptisādhakaṃ kiñcit pramāṇaṃ śaraṇabhūtam asti / tasmād vidhyor eva vyāptisādhakaṃ pramāṇam abhāvayor api vyāptisādhakam iti nyāyasya duratikramatvāt sattvābhāvena kramākramābhāvo vyāpta eveti nānaikāntika ity anavadyo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tad ayam akṣaṇikād vinivartamāṇaḥ svavyāpyaṃ sattvaṃ nivartya kṣaṇike viśrāmayatīti sattvahetoḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir apy anavadyā. /
body.translated_text: For the very same perception-natured <s>pramāṇa</s> by which — due to the absence of any other mode — the pervasion of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>), which is a positive entity, with successive and simultaneous [activity], which are positive entities, is established — by that very [<s>pramāṇa</s>] the pervasion of the absence of successive and simultaneous [activity] with the absence of causal efficacy must also be accepted. For there is no other <s>pramāṇa</s> serving as a refuge that establishes the pervasion of the absence of fire and the like with the absence of smoke and the like, apart from the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the pervasion of smoke and the like with fire and the like. Therefore, since the principle is inescapable that the very <s>pramāṇa</s> which establishes pervasion between positive [entities] also establishes pervasion between their absences, the absence of successive and simultaneous [activity] is pervaded by the absence of existence — thus [the reason] is not inconclusive, and the non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) is faultless. Therefore, this [non-perception of the pervader], withdrawing from the non-momentary and removing its pervaded [property] of existence, brings it to rest in the momentary — thus the proof of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) through the reason of existence is also faultless.

body.text: (78.10) nanu vyāpakānupalambhataḥ sattvasya kathaṃ svasādhyapratibandhasiddhiḥ, asyāpy anekadoṣaduṣṭatvāt / tathā hi na tāvad ayaṃ prasaṅga hetuḥ / sādhyadharmiṇi pramāṇasiddhatvāt, parābhyupagamasiddhatvābhāvāt, viparyayaparyavasānābhāvāc ca / atha svatantraḥ, tadāśrayāsiddhaḥ / akṣaṇikasyāśrayasyāsambhavāt / apratītatvād vā / pratītir hi pratyakṣeṇānumānena vikalpamātreṇa vā syāt /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, how is the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) of existence with its own <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) established through the non-perception of the pervader, since this [argument] too is vitiated by many faults? For, to begin with, this is not a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) reason, because it is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> in the property-bearer of the <s>sādhya</s>, because it is not established through the opponent's concession, and because it does not terminate in the contrary [of what is desired]. If then it is an independent [reason], it is unestablished as to its substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>), because the non-momentary substratum does not exist. Or [it is unestablished] because it is not cognized. For cognition [of the substratum] could be either by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), by inference (<s>anumāna</s>), or by mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>).

body.text: (79.1) prathamapakṣadvaye sākṣātpāramparyeṇa vā svapratītilakṣaṇārthakāritve maulaḥ sādhāraṇo hetuḥ vyāpakānupalambhaś ca svarūpāsiddhaḥ syāt / arthakriyākāritve kramākramayor anyatarasyāvaśyambhāvāt /
body.translated_text: In the first two alternatives, whether directly or indirectly, if [the substratum has] the capacity to produce its own cognized characteristic object, both the main common reason and the non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) would be unestablished in their own nature (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because one of either successive or simultaneous [causal activity] would necessarily obtain in [something having] causal efficacy.

body.text: (79.4) antimapakṣe tu na kaścid dhetur anāśrayaḥ syāt / vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāt /
body.translated_text: But in the last alternative, no reason would be without a substratum, because a property-bearer established by mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is easily available everywhere.

body.text: (79.6) api ca, tat kalpanājñānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvi vā syāt, liṅgajanma vā, saṃskārajaṃ vā, sandigdhavastukaṃ vā, avastukaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: (79.6) Moreover, that conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanājñāna</s>) [which allegedly contradicts momentariness] would either (1) follow upon direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), or (2) arise from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), or (3) arise from dispositional impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), or (4) have a doubtful object, or (5) have no object at all.

body.text: (79.8) tatrādyapakṣadvaye 'kṣaṇikasya sattaivāvyāhatā / kathaṃ bādhakāvatāraḥ /
body.translated_text: (79.8) Among these, in the first two alternatives, the very existence of the non-momentary is uncontradicted. How then can the contradicting [cognition] enter?

body.text: (79.9) tṛītye tu na sarvadā 'kṣaṇikasattāniṣedhaḥ / tadarpitasaṃskārābhāve tat smaraṇāyogāt /
body.translated_text: (79.9) In the third [alternative], the denial of the existence of the non-momentary does not hold always — because in the absence of dispositional impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by it, there could be no memory of it.

body.text: (79.10) caturthe tu sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ hetudoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: (79.10) In the fourth, having a doubtful basis (<s>sandigdhāśrayatva</s>) is a defect of the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>).

body.text: (79.11) pañcame ca tadviṣayasyābhāvo na tāvad pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati / akṣaṇikātmanaḥ sarvadaiva tvanmate 'pratyakṣatvāt na cānumānatas tadabhāvas tatpratibaddhaliṅgān upalam bhādityāśrayāsiddhis tāvad uddhatā / evaṃ dṛṣṭānto 'pi pratihantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: (79.11) In the fifth, the absence of the object of that [cognition] is not established through perception — since on your view the non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>) is never perceptible. Nor is its absence [established] through inference, since there is no apprehension of a logical mark connected to it — and so the fault of unestablished basis (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) is raised. Similarly, the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) should also be refuted.

body.text: (79.14) svarūpāsiddho 'py ayaṃ hetūḥ / sthirasyāpi kramākramisahakāryapekṣayā kramākramābhyām arthakriyopapatteḥ / nāpi kramayaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ / tathā hi kramisahakāryapekṣayā kramikāryakāritvan tāvad aviruddham /
body.translated_text: (79.14) This logical reason (<s>hetu</s>) is also unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>). For even of a permanent thing, causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is possible both sequentially and simultaneously, depending on sequential and simultaneous auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>). Nor is there the consequence of the faults stated in the sequential and simultaneous alternatives. For causal efficacy in sequence, depending on sequential auxiliary conditions, is not contradictory.

body.text: (79.17) tathā ca śaṃkarasya saṃkṣipto 'yam abhiprāyaḥ / sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyam / tadvaikalyaṃ cāsāmarthyam / na ca tayor āvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyān tadvataḥ kā cit kṣatiḥ / tasya tābhyām anyatvāt / tat kathaṃ sahakāriṇo 'napekṣa kāryakaraṇaprasaṅga iti /
body.translated_text: (79.17) And thus the summary of <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s view is as follows: The totality of auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakāri-sākalya</s>) is capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>), and their incompleteness is incapacity. The appearance and disappearance of those [auxiliary conditions] causes no damage to the entity possessing them, since it is different from them. Then how would there be the consequence of producing the effect without depending on auxiliary conditions?

body.text: (79.20) trilocanasyāpy ayaṃ saṃkṣiptārthaḥ / kāryam eva hi sahakāriṇam apekṣate / na ca kāryotpattihetuḥ / yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijam āgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaram, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavat sahakārinānātvād api kramavat kāryanānātvopapatter aśakyaṃ bhāvānām pratikṣaṇam anyonyatvam upapādayitum iti /
body.translated_text: (79.20) The summary meaning of <s>Trilocana</s> too is this: It is the effect alone that depends on auxiliary conditions, not [the capacity that is] the cause of the effect's arising. Since capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is twofold — innate (<s>nija</s>) and adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>), i.e., another auxiliary condition — therefore, even for a non-momentary entity, just as there is diversity of effects due to the diversity of auxiliary conditions occurring in sequence, it is impossible to demonstrate that things are different from one another at every moment.

body.text: (79.24) nyāyabhūṣaṇo 'pi lapati / prathamakāryotpādanakāle hi uttarakāryotpādanasvabhāvaḥ / ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryāṇi kuryād iti cet /
body.translated_text: (79.24) <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> also argues: At the time of producing the first effect, [the entity] has the nature of producing the later effect too. Therefore, it should produce all effects at the very first moment.

body.text: (79.26) tad idaṃ mātā me vandhyety ādivat svavacanavirodhād ayuktam / yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa katham ādau tat kāryaṃ kuryāt / na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ / na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikam api karotīti /
body.translated_text: (79.26) This is inappropriate — like saying "my mother is barren," it contradicts one's own statement (<s>svavacanavirodha</s>). For that which has the nature of producing the later effect — how would it produce that effect at the beginning? It would then not have the nature of producing that effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and the like.

body.text: (80.1) vācaspatir api paṭhati / nanv ayam akṣaṇikaḥ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati / tac cāsya svarūpaṃ tṛtīyādiṣiva kṣaṇeṣu dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe sad iti tadāpi janayet / akurvan vā tṛtīyādiṣv api na kurvīta / tasya tādāvasthyāt / atādavasthye vā tad evāsya kṣaṇikatvam /
body.translated_text: (80.1) <s>Vācaspati</s> also argues: This non-momentary entity produces the effect by its own nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). And that nature of its, being present in the second moment just as in the third and subsequent moments, should produce [the effect] then too. Or if not producing [in the second moment], it should not produce in the third and subsequent moments either — because of the entity's being in the same condition (<s>tādāvasthya</s>). Or if not in the same condition, that itself is its momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>).

body.text: (80.4) atrocyate / satyaṃ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati na tu tenaiva / sahakārisahitād eva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāt / tasmād vyāptivatkāryakāraṇabhāvo 'py ekatrānyayogavyavacchedena / anyatrāyogavyavacchedenanāvaboddhavyaḥ / tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ sampratipatter iti na kramikāryakāritvapakṣoktadoṣāvasaraḥ /
body.translated_text: (80.4) To this it is replied: True, it produces the effect by its own nature, but not by that alone — because the effect is observed to arise from that [nature] only when accompanied by auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>). Therefore, like pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), the cause-effect relation too is to be understood through the positive determination "only in connection with the other" in one case, and through the negative determination "not without it" in the other. Since this is the settled understanding of ordinary people and critical examiners alike, there is no occasion for the faults stated in the sequential-effect alternative.

body.text: (80.8) nāpy akṣaṇike yaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣāvakāśaḥ / ye hi kāryam utpāditavanto dravyaviśeṣās teṣāṃ vyāpārasya niyatakāryotpādanasamarthasya niṣpādite kārye 'nuvartamāneṣv api teṣu dravyeṣu nivṛttārthād ūnā sāmagrī jāyate / tat kathaṃ niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayiṣyati / na hi daṇḍādayaḥ svabhāvenaiva kartāro yenāmi niṣpatter ārabhya kāryaṃ vidadhyuḥ / kiṃ tarhi vyāpārāveśinaḥ / na ceyatā svarūpeṇa na kartāraḥ / svarūpakārakatvanirvāhaparatayā vyāpārasamāveśād iti /
body.translated_text: (80.8) Nor is there occasion for the faults stated in the simultaneity alternative for the non-momentary. For those particular substances that have produced the effect — when their operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), which was capable of producing the specific effect, has accomplished the effect — even while those substances continue to exist, the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) becomes deficient because its purpose has been fulfilled. How then will it produce again what has already been produced? For sticks and the like are not producers by their very nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) such that they would create an effect from the very start. Rather, they are producers through the application of operation. And it is not that by this much they are not producers by their own nature — rather, operation is applied in order to accomplish the production that is [effected] through their own nature.

body.text: (80.13) kiṃ ca kramākramābhāvaś ca bhaviṣyati / na ca sattvābhāva iti sandigdhavyatireko 'py ayaṃ vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / na hi kramākramābhyām anyasya prakārasyābhāvaḥ siddhaḥ / viśeṣaniṣedhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāt /
body.translated_text: (80.13) Moreover, the absence of both succession (<s>krama</s>) and simultaneity (<s>akrama</s>) will result. And this non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) has doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>), since it is not [established that] there is no existence (<s>sattva</s>). For the absence of any other mode besides succession and simultaneity is not established, since a specific negation has as its scope the permission of the remainder.

body.text: (80.16) kiṃ ca prakārāntarasya dṛśyatve nātyantaniṣedhaḥ / adṛśyatve tu nāsattāniścayo viprakarṣiṇām iti na kramākramābhyām arthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptisiddhiḥ / ataḥ sandigdhavyatireko 'pi vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: (80.16) Moreover, if the other mode is perceptible, there is no absolute negation. But if it is imperceptible, then for those at a great distance there is no ascertainment of non-existence—hence the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the capacity for efficient action (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>) by succession and simultaneity is not established. Therefore, this too is a non-perception of the pervader with doubtful negative concomitance.

body.text: (80.19) kiṃ ca dṛśyādṛśyasahakāripratyayasākalyavataḥ kramayaugapadyasyātyantaparokṣatvāt tena vyāptaṃ sattvam api parokṣam eveti na tāvat pratibandhaḥ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati / nāpy anumānataḥ / tatpratibaddhaliṅgābhāvād iti /
body.translated_text: (80.19) Moreover, since the succession and simultaneity of [an entity] possessing the totality of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakāripratyaya</s>), both visible and invisible, is completely beyond perception (<s>parokṣa</s>), existence (<s>sattva</s>) pervaded by that is also beyond perception. Hence the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is not established through perception, nor through inference, due to the absence of a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) bound to that [connection].

body.text: (80.22) api ca kramākramābhyām arthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptam ity atisubhāṣitam / yadi krameṇa vyāptaṃ katham akrameṇa, athākrameṇa na tarhi krameṇa / kramākramābhyāṃ vyāptim iti tu bruvatā vyāpter evābhāvaḥ pradarśito bhavati / na hi bhavaty agnir dhūmabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ vyāpta iti / ato vyāpter anaikāntikatvam /
body.translated_text: (80.22) Moreover, it is exceedingly well said that efficient causal action (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) is pervaded by succession and simultaneity! If it is pervaded by succession, how [also] by non-succession? If by non-succession, then not by succession. But one who says it is "pervaded by both succession and non-succession" has actually demonstrated the very absence of pervasion. For it is not the case that fire is pervaded by both the presence and absence of smoke. Therefore, the pervasion is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: (80.26) api ca kim idaṃ bādhakam akṣaṇikānām asattāṃ sādhayati / utasvid akṣaṇikāt sattvasya vyatirekam / atha sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ pratibandham /
body.translated_text: (80.26) Moreover, does this sublating [argument] prove the non-existence (<s>asattā</s>) of non-momentary entities? Or the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of existence (<s>sattva</s>) from non-momentary [entities]? Or the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) between existence and momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>)?

body.text: (80.28) na pūrvo vikalpaḥ / uktakrameṇa hetor āśrayāsiddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: (80.28) The first alternative is not [valid], because the reason has an unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>), in the manner previously stated.

body.text: (80.29) na ca dvitīyaḥ / yato vyāpakanivṛttisahitā vyāpyanivṛttir vyatirekaśabdasyārthaḥ / sā ca yadi pratyakṣeṇa pratīyate tadā taddhetuḥ syād iti sattvam anaikāntikam / vyāpakānupalambhaḥ svarūpāsiddhiḥ / atha sā vikalpyate tadā pūrvoktakrameṇa pañcadhā vikalpya vikalpo dūṣaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: (80.29) Nor is the second, because the cessation of the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) conjoined with the cessation of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is the meaning of the word <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance). If that is perceived through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), then that would be its reason, and existence (<s>sattva</s>) would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). The non-perception of the pervader would have an unestablished own-nature (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>). If, however, that is conceptually constructed (<s>vikalpya</s>), then the conceptual construction is to be refuted in five ways in the manner previously stated.

body.text: (81.1) ata eva na tṛtīyo 'pi vikalpaḥ / vyatirekāsiddhau sambandhāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: (81.1) For this very reason, the third alternative too is not [valid], since when negative concomitance is unestablished, the relation (<s>sambandha</s>) is unestablished.

body.text: (81.2) kiṃ ca na bhūtalavad atrākṣaṇiko dharmi dṛśyate / na ca svabhāvānupalambhe vyāpakānupalambhaḥ kasya cit dṛśyasya pratipattim antareṇāntarbhāvayituṃ śakyata iti /
body.translated_text: (81.2) Moreover, no non-momentary property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is observed here, as a patch of ground is observed. And when one's own nature is not perceived, the non-perception of the pervader cannot be subsumed without the cognition of something perceptible.

body.text: (81.4) kiṃ cāsyābhāvadharmatve āśrayāsiddhatvam itaretarāśrayatvaṃ ca / bhāvadharmatve viruddhatvaṃ ca / ubhayadharmatve cānaikāntikatvam iti na trayīṃ doṣajātim atipatati /
body.translated_text: (81.4) Moreover, if this [reason] has the property of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), there is the defect of unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddhatva</s>) and mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśrayatva</s>). If it has the property of [positive] existence, there is contradiction (<s>viruddhatva</s>). And if it has both properties, there is inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>). Thus it does not escape the three classes of defects (<s>doṣajāti</s>).

body.text: (81.6) yat punar uktam akṣaṇikatve kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhād iti / tatra virodhasiddhim anusaratā virodhy api pratipattavyaḥ / tatpratītināntarīyakatvād virodhasiddheḥ / yathā tuhinadahanayoḥ sāpekṣadhruvabhāvayoś ca /
body.translated_text: (81.6) Now, as for what was stated—"in the case of non-momentariness, there is a contradiction with efficient action through succession and simultaneity"—therein, by one who follows the establishment of the contradiction (<s>virodha</s>), the contradictory [i.e., the permanent entity] must also be cognized, since the establishment of contradiction is inseparable from its cognition. Just as with cold and fire, and with entities that are permanent relative to their dependents.

body.text: (81.8) pratiyogī cākṣaṇikaḥ pratīyamānaḥ pratītikāritvāt sann eva syāt ajanakasyāprameyatvāt /
body.translated_text: (81.8) And the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>)—the non-momentary [entity]—when cognized, would be existent (<s>sat</s>) precisely because of being a cause of cognition, since what is not a producer is not a valid object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>).

body.text: (81.10) saṃvṛtisiddhenākṣaṇikatvena virodhasiddhir iti cet / saṃvṛtisiddham api vāstavaṃ kālpanikaṃ vā syāt /
body.translated_text: (81.10) [Objection:] The establishment of contradiction is through conventionally established (<s>saṃvṛtisiddha</s>) non-momentariness. [Reply:] Even what is conventionally established must be either real (<s>vāstava</s>) or constructed (<s>kālpanika</s>).

body.text: (81.12) yadi vāstavaṃ kathaṃ tasyāsattvam / kathaṃ cārthakriyākāritvavirodhaḥ / arthakriyāṃ kurvad dhi vāstavam ucyate /
body.translated_text: (81.12) If it is real, how can it be non-existent? And how can it contradict efficient causal action (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>)? For what performs efficient action is called real.

body.text: (81.14) atha kālpanikam / tatra kiṃ virodho vāstavaḥ, kālpaniko vā / na tāvad vāstavaḥ / kalpitavirodhivirodhatvāt, vandhyāputravirodhavat / atha virodho 'pi kālpanikaḥ / na tarhi sattvasya vyatirekaḥ pāramārthika iti kṣaṇabhaṅgo dattajalāñjalir iti /
body.translated_text: (81.14) If it is constructed—then is the contradiction real or constructed? It is not real, because it would be a contradiction with a constructed contradictory, like the contradiction with the son of a barren woman. If the contradiction too is constructed, then the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of existence is not ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>)—and so momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) has offered its parting libation.

body.text: (81.17) ayam eva codyaprabandho 'smad gurūbhiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ /
body.translated_text: (81.17) This very series of objections has been compiled by our teacher(s).

body.text: (81.18) nityaṃ nāsti na vā pratītiviṣayas tenāśrayāsiddhatā hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatir ataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca / śūnyaṃ ca dvitayena sidhyati na cāsattāpi sattā yathā no nityena virodhasiddhir asatā śakṣā kramāder api / iti (kṣaṇabhaṅgādhyāye) /
body.translated_text: (81.18) [Verse:] The permanent either does not exist or is not an object of cognition; hence the locus of the reason is unestablished, and one's own experience is damaged; the positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) too is thereby rejected. The void [of the permanent] is not established by both [means]; non-existence is not [established] like existence. Nor is the establishment of contradiction possible with the permanent—incapable even of succession and the like. Thus [ends the section] in the Chapter on Momentary Destruction (<s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgādhyāya</s>).

body.text: (81.23) atrocyate / iha vastuny api dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭo yathā gavi gotvam, paṭe śuklatvam turage gamanam ityādi / avastuny api dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭo yathā śaśaviṣāṇe tīkṣṇatvābhāvo vandhyāputre vaktṛtvābhāvo gaganāravinde gandhābhāva ityādi / tatrāvastuni dharmitvaṃ nāstīti kiṃ vastudharmeṇa dharmitvaṃ nāsti / āhosvid avastudharmeṇāpi /
body.translated_text: (81.23) To this it is replied: Here, even in real entities (<s>vastu</s>), the convention of property-bearer and property (<s>dharmin-dharma</s>) is observed — as in [the case of] cowness in a cow, whiteness in cloth, movement in a horse, and so on. And even in non-entities (<s>avastu</s>), the convention of property-bearer and property is observed — as in [the case of] the absence of sharpness in a hare's horn, the absence of speaking in a barren woman's son, the absence of fragrance in a sky-lotus, and so on. Now, [regarding] the assertion that non-entities cannot be property-bearers: does this mean that they cannot be property-bearers with respect to a real property (<s>vastudharma</s>), or that they cannot be property-bearers even with respect to a non-real property (<s>avastudharma</s>)?

body.text: (81.27) prathamapakṣe siddhasādhanam / dvitīyapakṣe tu svavacanavirodhaḥ / yad āhur guravaḥ //
body.translated_text: (81.27) In the first alternative, what is to be proved is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). In the second alternative, there is a contradiction with one's own statement (<s>svavacanavirodha</s>). As the venerable teachers have stated:

body.text: (81.28) dharmasya kasya cid avastuni mānasiddhā bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kim ihāsti no vā kvāpy asti cet katham iyanti na dūṣaṇāni nāsty eva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: (81.28) 'With regard to some property of a non-entity, is it the case that the convention of sublation (<s>bādhā</s>) or establishment (<s>vidhi</s>), validated by a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), exists here or does it not? If it exists somewhere, then how [can you avoid] these many faults? If it does not exist at all, then the consequence of contradicting one's own statement is established.'

body.text: (82.1) avastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvasya vyāpakasyābhāvād āśrayāsiddhidūṣaṇasyānupanyāsaprasaṅga ity arthaḥ / yenaiva hi vacanenāvastuno dharmitvaṃ pratiṣidhyate / tenaivāvastuno dharmitvābhāvena dharmeṇa dharmitvam abhyupagatam / paraṃ tu pratiṣidhyata iti vyaktam idam īśvaraceṣṭitam / tathā hy avastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanena dharmitvābhāvaḥ kim avastuni vidhīyata, anyatra vā, na vā kva cid apīti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: (82.1) The meaning is: since the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) — namely, the prior acceptance of the property-bearer status of a non-entity — is absent, there would be the absurd consequence of never adducing the fallacy of unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>). For by the very statement by which the property-bearer status of a non-entity is denied, by that very statement the property-bearer status of the non-entity is accepted — through the property of the absence of property-bearer status in the non-entity. But it is the other [party's position] that is being denied — this is clearly a divine performance (<s>īśvaraceṣṭita</s>). For by the statement 'the non-entity has no property-bearer status,' [we ask:] is the absence of property-bearer status predicated of the non-entity, or of something else, or of nothing at all? — these are three alternatives.

body.text: (82.6) prathamapakṣe 'vastuno na dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ / dharmitvābhāvasya dharmasya tatraiva vidhānāt /
body.translated_text: (82.6) In the first alternative, there is no denial of property-bearer status for the non-entity — because the property of 'absence of property-bearer status' is predicated right there [in the non-entity itself].

body.text: (82.7) dvitīye 'vastuni kimāyātam / anyatra dharmitvābhāvavidhānāt /
body.translated_text: (82.7) In the second alternative, what relevance is there to the non-entity? — since the absence of property-bearer status is predicated of something else.

body.text: (82.8) tṛtīyas tu pakṣo vyartha eva nirāśrayatvād iti katham avastuno dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ / tasmād yathā pramāṇopanyāsaḥ prameyatvasvīkāra pūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ, vācakaśabdopanyāso vā vācyasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptas tathā 'vastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanopanyāso 'vastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ / anyathā tadvacanopanyāsasya vyarthatvāt /
body.translated_text: (82.8) And the third alternative is simply pointless, since it has no locus. So how can the property-bearer status of a non-entity be denied? Therefore, just as the adduction of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is pervaded by the prior acceptance of something as an object of valid knowledge (<s>prameyatva</s>), or just as the adduction of a denoting word is pervaded by the prior acceptance of something as denotable — so too the adduction of the statement 'the non-entity has no property-bearer status' is pervaded by the prior acceptance of property-bearer status for the non-entity. Otherwise, the adduction of that statement would be pointless.

body.text: (82.11) tad yadi vacanopanyāso vyāpyadharmas tadā 'vastuno dharmitvasvīkāro 'pi vyāpakadharmo durvāraḥ / atha na vyāpakadharmaḥ, tadā vyāpyasyāpi vacanopanyāsasyāsambhava iti mūkataivātra balād āyāteti kathaṃ na svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: (82.11) Therefore, if the adduction of the statement is the pervaded property (<s>vyāpyadharma</s>), then the acceptance of property-bearer status for the non-entity, as the pervading property (<s>vyāpakadharma</s>), is unavoidable. But if it is not the pervading property, then even the pervaded — namely, the adduction of the statement — is impossible. And so muteness forcibly ensues here. How, then, is there not a demonstration of contradiction with one's own statement?

body.text: (82.15) yad āhācāryaḥ / na hy abruvan paraṃ bodhayitum īśaḥ / [a]bruvan vā doṣam imaṃ parihartum iti mahati saṃkaṭe praveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: (82.15) As the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) has said: 'For one who does not speak cannot make another understand; but one who speaks cannot avoid this fault. Thus there is entry into a great impasse.'

body.text: (82.17) avastuprastāve sahṛdayānāṃ mūkataiva yujyate iti cet / aho mahad vaidagdhyam / avastuprastāve svayam eva yathāśakti valgitvā bhagno mūkataiva nyāyaprāpteti paribhāyayā niḥsartum icchati / na cāvastuprastāvo rājadaṇḍena vinā caraṇamardanādināniṣṭimātreṇa vā pratiṣedhuṃ śakṣate / tataś cātrāpi kramākramabhāvasya sādhanatve sattvābhāvasya ca sādhyatve sandigdhavastubhāvasyāvastvātmano vā kṣaṇikasya dharmitvaṃ kena pratiṣidhyate /
body.translated_text: (82.17) [Objection:] In the discussion of non-entities, muteness alone is appropriate for the discerning. — [Reply:] Oh, what great cleverness! Having himself, to the best of his ability, pranced about in the discussion of non-entities and then been defeated, he now wishes to escape through the embarrassment [of claiming that] 'muteness alone is the proper course!' But the discussion of non-entities cannot be prohibited by mere disapproval — like foot-stamping, without the king's punishment. Therefore, even here, when sequential-and-simultaneous existence is being proved and the absence of existence (<s>sattvābhāva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), and when the property-bearer is a momentary entity (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) whose entity-status is doubtful or whose nature is non-entity — who can deny its property-bearer status?

body.text: (82.22) trividho hi dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ / kaś cit vastuniyato nīlādiḥ / kaś cid avastuniyato yathā sarvopākhyāvirahaḥ / kaś cid ubhayasādhāraṇo yathā 'nupalabdhimātram / tatra vastudharmeṇāvastuno dharmitvaniṣedha iti yuktam / na tv avastudharmeṇa / vastvavastudharmeṇa vā / svavacanasyānupanyāsaprasaṅgād ity akṣaṇikasyābhāve sandehe 'pi vā 'vastudharmeṇa dharmitvam avyāhatam iti nāyam āśrayāsiddho vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: (82.22) For properties (<s>dharma</s>) are observed to be of three kinds: some are restricted to real entities (<s>vastu</s>), such as blue and the like; some are restricted to non-entities (<s>avastu</s>), such as the absence of all designations; and some are common to both, such as mere non-perception (<s>anupalabdhimātra</s>). Therein, the denial of property-bearer status for a non-entity with respect to a real property — that is justified. But not with respect to a non-real property, nor with respect to a property common to both real and non-real. [For otherwise,] there would be the absurd consequence of not adducing one's own statement [which itself predicates something of a non-entity]. Therefore, even when the non-momentary is absent or [its existence is merely] doubtful, its property-bearer status through a non-real property is unimpeded. Hence this non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) does not have an unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>).

body.text: (82.27) akṣaṇikāpratītāvāśrayasiddho hetur iti yuktam uktām / tadapratītau tadvyavahārāyogāt / kevalam asau vyavahārāṅgabhūtā pratītir vastvavastunor ekarūpā na bhavati / sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vastusāmarthyabhāvinī hi vastupratītiḥ / yathā pratyakṣam anumānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvi ca vikalpaḥ / avastunas tu sāmarthyābhāvād vikalpamātram eva pratītiḥ / vastuno hi vastubalabhāvinī pratītir yathā sākṣāt pratyakṣam, paramparayā tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo 'numānaṃ ca / avastuno na vastubalabhāvinī pratītis tatkārakatvenāvastutvahāniprasaṅgāt / tasmād vikalpamātram evāvastunaḥ pratītiḥ /
body.translated_text: (82.27) When the non-momentary is not cognized, the reason is said to be established in its substratum (<s>āśrayasiddha</s>) — this has been rightly stated. Because in the absence of its cognition, the conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) regarding it would be impossible. However, that cognition, which is a constituent of conventional usage, is not of the same kind for a real entity (<s>vastu</s>) and a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>). For the cognition of a real entity arises from the power of the real entity itself, either directly or indirectly — as, for example, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) that follows upon perception. But for a non-entity, since there is no [causal] power, mere conceptual construction alone is its cognition. For the cognition of a real entity arises from the force of reality: directly, as perception; indirectly, as conceptual construction that follows upon [perception] and inference. The cognition of a non-entity does not arise from the force of reality — because, if it were a cause [i.e., had causal power], there would be the unwanted consequence of its ceasing to be a non-entity. Therefore, mere conceptual construction alone is the cognition of a non-entity.

body.text: (83.4) na hy abhāvah kaś cid vigrahavān yaḥ sākṣātkartavyo 'pi tu vyavahartavyaḥ / sa ca vyavahāro vikalpād api sidhyaty eva / anyathā sarvajanaprasiddho 'vastuvyavahāro na syāt / iṣyate ca /
body.translated_text: (83.4) For absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is not some embodied thing that is to be directly perceived; rather, it is to be dealt with in conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>). And that conventional usage is accomplished even through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. Otherwise, the universally recognized conventional usage regarding non-entities would not be possible. And it is indeed accepted [by all].

body.text: (83.6) taddharmitvapratiṣedhānubandhād ity akāmenāpi vikalpamātrasiddho 'kṣaṇikaḥ svīkartavya iti nāyam apratītatvād apy āśrayāsiddho hetur vaktavyaḥ / tataś cākṣaṇikasya vikalpamātrasiddhatve yad uktam /
body.translated_text: (83.6) Since [the opponent's argument] is connected with the denial of [the non-momentary's] being a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — even unwillingly, the non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>), established by mere conceptual construction, must be accepted. Therefore, this reason is not to be called unestablished in its substratum even though [the non-momentary is] not cognized [by perception]. And since the non-momentary is established by mere conceptual construction, what was stated —

body.text: (83.9) na kaś cid dhetur anāśrayaḥ vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvād iti /
body.translated_text: (83.9) 'No reason is without a substratum, because a property-bearer established by mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is easily available everywhere' —

body.text: (83.10) tad asaṅgatam / vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sambhave 'pi vastudharmeṇa dharmitvāyogāt / vastudharmahetutvāpekṣaya āśrayāsiddhasyāpi hetoḥ sambhavāt /
body.translated_text: (83.10) That is incoherent. Even though a property-bearer established by mere conceptual construction is possible everywhere, it cannot serve as a property-bearer with respect to a real property (<s>vastudharma</s>). Because, with respect to a real-property reason, even a reason that is unestablished in its substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>) is possible [as a fault].

body.text: (83.11) yathā ātmano vibhutvasādhanārtham upanyastaṃ sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvād iti sādhanam / vikalpaś cāyaṃ hetūpanyāsāt / pūrvaṃ sandigdhavastukaḥ / samarthite tu hetāv avastuka iti brūmaḥ /
body.translated_text: (83.11) Just as the proof advanced for establishing the all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) of the self (<s>ātman</s>) — 'because it possesses qualities that are perceived everywhere' — [illustrates this point]. And this conceptual construction [of the non-momentary], prior to the presentation of the reason, has a doubtful real object. But when the reason is validated, we say it is without a real object (<s>avastuka</s>).

body.text: (83.14) na cātra sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ nāma hetudoṣaḥ / āstāṃ tāvat / sandigdhasyāvastuno 'pi vikalpamātrasiddhasyāvastudharmāpekṣayā dharmitvaprasādhanāt / vastudharmahetvapekṣayaiva sandigdhāśrayasya hetvābhāsasya vyavasthāpanāt / yatheha nikuñje mayūraḥ kekāyitād iti / avastukavikalpaviṣayasyāsattvaṃ tu vyāpakānupalambhād eva prasādhitam / evaṃ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi vyomotpalāder dharmitvaṃ vikalpamātreṇa pratītiś cāvagantavyā / tad evam avastudharmāpekṣayā 'vastunodharmitvasya vikalpamātreṇa pratīteś cāpahnotum aśakyatvān nāyam āśrayāsiddho hetuḥ / na ca dṛṣṭāntakṣatiḥ /
body.translated_text: (83.14) Nor is 'having a doubtful substratum' (<s>sandigdhāśrayatva</s>) here a defect of the reason. Let that be, for the time being — because even for a non-entity that is doubtful [as to real existence], established by mere conceptual construction, its being a property-bearer with respect to non-entity properties is established. Because the pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) characterized as having a doubtful substratum is determined only with respect to a real-property reason — as, for example, 'there is a peacock in this thicket, because of the cry.' But the non-existence of the object of that conceptual construction of the non-momentary, which is without real basis — that is established through the non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) itself. Likewise, the property-bearerhood of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) too — such as the sky-lotus and the like — and its cognition should be understood as [obtained] through mere conceptual construction alone. Thus, since the property-bearerhood of a non-entity with respect to non-entity properties and its cognition through mere conceptual construction cannot be denied, this is not a reason with an unestablished substratum. Nor is the example damaged.

body.text: (83.20) na caiṣa svarūpāsiddhaḥ / akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramayor vyāpakayor ayogāt / tathā hi yadi tasya prathame kṣaṇe dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇasāmarthyam asti tadā prathamakṣaṇabhāvikāryavat dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvyam api (?) kāryaṃ kuryāt / samarthasya kṣepāyogāt /
body.translated_text: (83.20) Nor is this [reason] unestablished in its own form (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>). Because in a non-momentary property-bearer, the conjunction of successive (<s>krama</s>) and simultaneous (<s>akrama</s>) [causal activity], which are pervaders (<s>vyāpaka</s>), is impossible. For if [the non-momentary entity] has in its first moment the capacity to produce effects that occur in the second and subsequent moments, then it should produce the effect occurring in the second and subsequent moments just as it produces the effect occurring in the first moment — because it is impossible for a capable [entity] to defer [its action].

body.text: (83.22) atha tadā sahakārisākalyalakṣaṇasāmarthyaṃ nāsti / tadvaikalyalakṣaṇasyāsāmarthyasya sambhavāt / na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti / sahakārisahitād eva tataḥ kāryotpattidarsanāt iti cet /
body.translated_text: (83.22) [Objection:] If at that time the capacity characterized by the completeness of auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakāri-sākalya</s>) is not present — because the incapacity characterized by their incompleteness is possible — [the entity] does not produce by its own nature alone; rather, it produces precisely through its own nature [in conjunction with auxiliaries], since the effect is observed to arise only from [the cause] accompanied by auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>) —

body.text: (83.24) yadā tāvad amī militāḥ santaḥ kāryaṃ kurvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam eṣām astu ko niṣeddhā / militair eva tu tatkāryaṃ karttavyam iti kuto labhyate / pūrvāparakālayor ekasvabhāvatvād bhāvasya / sarvadā jananājananayor anyataraniyamaprasaṅgasya durvāratvāt / tasmāt sāmagrī janikā naikaṃ janakam iti sthiravādināṃ manorājyasyāpy aviṣayaḥ /
body.translated_text: (83.24) [Reply:] When these [causes], having come together, produce the effect — let their cooperation, characterized as working toward a single purpose (<s>ekārthakaraṇa</s>), be so — who denies it? But from where is it obtained that the effect must be produced only by [all of] them together? Because the entity is of one and the same nature in earlier and later moments. Because the unwanted consequence — that either production or non-production must be invariably fixed at all times — is inescapable. Therefore, 'the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is the producer, not any single [entity] among them' — this is beyond even the realm of wishful thinking for the proponents of permanence.

body.text: (83.29) kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate tāvad evam iti cet / dṛśyatāṃ kiṃ tu pūrvasthitād eva paścāt sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭād bhāvāt kāryotpattir anyasmād eva viśiṣṭasāmagrīsamutpannāt kṣaṇād iti vivādapadam etat / tatra prāg api sambhave sarvadaiva kāryotpattir na vā kadā cid apīti virodham asamādhāya tad eva kāryotpattir iti sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpām arhati /
body.translated_text: (83.29) [Objection:] What can we do? It is observed to be thus. — [Reply:] Let it be observed. But this is the very point of dispute: whether the effect arises from the very same entity that existed before and then entered into the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), or from a different entity — a distinct moment that has arisen from the specific aggregate. Without resolving the contradiction that "if [causal efficacy was] possible even before, the effect should always arise, or never at all" — one who proceeds by merely restating the thesis (<s>sādhyānuvāda</s>), saying "the effect arises from that very [permanent entity]," deserves pity.

body.text: (84.3) na ca pratyabhijñānād evaikatvasiddhiḥ / tat pauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśakuśakadalīstambādau nirdalanāt / vistareṇa ca pratyabhijñādūṣaṇam asmābhiḥ sthirasiddhidūṣaṇe pratipāditam iti tad evāvadhāryam /
body.translated_text: (84.3) Nor is identity [of the entity across time] established from recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) alone. For that [recognition] is refuted — [the recognition being merely] of human origin (<s>pauruṣa</s>) — in the case of cut hair that regrows, <s>kuśa</s> grass, plantain trunks, and the like. Moreover, the refutation of recognition has been presented by us in detail in the "Refutation of the Proof of Permanence" (<s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s>), and that should be consulted.

body.text: (84.6) nanu kāryam eva sahakāriṇam apekṣate / na tu kāryotpattihetuḥ / yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijam āgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaraṃ, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavat sahakārinānātvād api kramavat kāryanānātvam iti cet /
body.translated_text: (84.6) [Objection:] It is the effect alone that depends on auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>), not [the capacity that is] the cause of the effect's arising. Since capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is twofold — innate (<s>nija</s>) and adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>), i.e., another auxiliary condition — therefore, even for a non-momentary entity, just as there is diversity of effects due to the diversity of auxiliary conditions occurring in sequence, there is diversity of effects.

body.text: (84.8) bhavatu tāvat nijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyam / tathāpi tat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ sadyaḥ kriyādharmakamavaśyābhyupagantavyam / tad yadi prāg api, prāg api kāryaprasaṅgaḥ / atha paścād eva, na tadā sthiro bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: (84.8) Let capacity indeed be twofold, with the distinction of innate and adventitious. Even so, that [capacity] must necessarily be accepted as a particular real entity (<s>vastu-svalakṣaṇa</s>) possessing the property of immediate causal activity (<s>sadyaḥ-kriyā</s>). If [it exists] before [the production], there would be the unwanted consequence of the effect occurring before. If [it arises] only afterwards, then the entity is not permanent.

body.text: (84.11) na ca kāryaṃ sahakāriṇo 'pekṣata iti yuktam, tasyāsattvāt / hetuś ca sann api yadi svakāryaṃ na karoti, tadā tatkāryam eva tan na syāt / svātantryāt /
body.translated_text: (84.11) Nor is it correct to say that the effect depends on auxiliary conditions, since [the effect] does not [yet] exist. And if the cause, though existing, does not produce its own effect, then it would not be the cause of that effect at all — due to its independence (<s>svātantrya</s>).

body.text: (84.13) yaccoktam / yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvah / sa katham ādau kāryaṃ kuryāt / na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ / na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikam api karotīti /
body.translated_text: (84.13) And what was said: "That which has the nature of producing the later effect — how would it produce that effect at the beginning? It would then not have the nature of producing that effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and the like."

body.text: (84.15) tad asaṅgatam / sthirasvabhāvatve bhāvasyottarakālam evedaṃ na pūrvakālam iti kuta etat / tadabhāvāc ca kāraṇam apy uttarakāryasvabhāvam ity api kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: (84.15) That is irrelevant. If the entity has a permanent nature, whence comes this [distinction]: "this [happens] only at the later time, not at the earlier time"? And without that [temporal distinction], whence even the claim that the cause has the nature of [producing] the later effect?

body.text: (84.17) kiṃ kurmaḥ / uttarakālam eva tasya janmeti cet / sthiratve tadanupapadyamānam asthiratām ādiśatu / sthiratve 'py eṣa eva svabhāvas tasya yad uttarakṣaṇa eva kāryaṃ karotīti cet / na, pramāṇabādhite svabhāvābhyupagamāyogād iti na tāvad akṣaṇikasya kramikāryakāritvam asti / nāpyakramikāryakāritvasambhavaḥ / dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe kārakasvarūpasadbhāve punar api kāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: (84.17) [Objection:] What can we do? Its production is only at the later time. — [Reply:] If that is inconsistent with permanence, let it indicate impermanence. [Objection:] Even in permanence, this is its very nature — that it produces the effect only at the later moment. — [Reply:] No, because it is untenable to accept a nature that is contradicted by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Thus, a non-momentary entity does not have sequential causal efficacy (<s>kramikāryakāritva</s>). Nor is simultaneous causal efficacy possible — because, if the producer's own nature persists even in the second moment, there would be the unwanted consequence of producing the effect again.

body.text: (84.21) kārye niṣpanne tadviṣayavyāpārābhāvād ūnā sāmagrī na niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayed iti cet / na, sāmagrīsambhavāsambhavayor api sadyaḥ kriyākārakasvarūpasambhave janakatvam avadhāryam iti prāg eva pratipādanāt / kāryasya hi niṣpāditatvāt punaḥ kartum aśakyatvam eva kāraṇam asamartham āvedayati /
body.translated_text: (84.21) [Objection:] When the effect has been accomplished, the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) directed toward it is absent, and so the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) becomes deficient — it will not produce what has already been produced. — [Reply:] No, because it has already been demonstrated that when the producer's own nature — capable of immediate activity — exists, whether or not the aggregate is present, production must be acknowledged. For the very fact that the effect, having been accomplished, cannot be produced again, itself reveals that the cause is incapable [at that point].

body.text: (84.23) tad ayam akṣaṇike kramākramikāryakāritvābhāvo na siddhaḥ / na ca kramākramābhyām aparaprakārasambhavo yena tābhyām avyāptau sandigdhavyatireko hetuḥ syāt / prakārāntaraśaṅkāyāṃ tasyāpi dṛśyatvādṛśyatvaprakāradvayadūṣaṇe 'pi svapakṣe 'py anāśvāsaprasaṅgāt / tasmād anyo 'nyavyavacchedasthitir nāparaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati / svarūpāpraviṣṭasya vastuno 'vastuno vā 'tatsvabhāvatvāt / prakārāntarasyāpi kramasvarūpāpraviṣṭatvāt / tathātīndriyasya sahakāriṇo 'dṛśyatve 'pyayogavyavacchedena dṛśyasahakārisahitasya sattvasya dṛśyakramākramābhyāṃ vyāptiḥ pratyakṣād eva sidhyati / evaṃ kramākramābhyām arthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptam iti kramākramayor anyo 'nyavyavacchedena sthitatvād etat prakāradvayaparihāreṇārthākriyakāritvam anyatra na gatam ity arthaḥ / ata evaitayor vinivṛttau nivartate /
body.translated_text: (84.23) Thus, this absence of both sequential and simultaneous causal efficacy in the non-momentary is not established [according to the opponent]. Nor is there any other possible mode besides sequential and simultaneous [activity], such that from non-pervasion by both there would be a reason with uncertain negative concomitance (<s>sandigdha-vyatireka</s>). For if another mode is suspected, the refutation through the two modes of visible and invisible [causal activity] would result in lack of confidence even in one's own thesis. Therefore, no other mode besides mutual exclusion (<s>anyonya-vyavaccheda-sthiti</s>) is possible — because what does not enter into a thing's own nature, whether a real entity or a non-entity, is not of that nature; and because any other mode also does not enter into the nature of sequence. Similarly, even when an imperceptible auxiliary condition is invisible, the pervasion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) — accompanied by visible auxiliary conditions — with visible sequential and simultaneous [activity] is established through perception alone, by the principle of negative determination (<s>ayoga-vyavaccheda</s>). Thus, since causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) is pervaded by sequential and simultaneous [activity], and since these two are established through mutual exclusion, the absence of causal efficacy does not go elsewhere beyond the elimination of these two modes — this is the meaning. And therefore, when these two are negated, [causal efficacy] ceases.

body.text: (85.4) trilocanasyāpi vikalpatraye prathamadūṣaṇam āśrayāsiddhidoṣaparihārato nirastam /
body.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>'s first objection too, among the three alternatives, is refuted through the removal of the fault of unestablished substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>).

body.text: (85.5) dvitīyaṃ cāsaṅgatam / vikalpajñānena vyatirekasya pratītatvāt / na hy abhāvaḥ kaś cid vigrahavān yaḥ sākṣatkartavyaḥ, api tu vikalpād eva vyavahartavyaḥ / na hy abhāvasya vikalpād anyāpratipattir apratipattir vā sarvathā / ubhayathāpi tadvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt / evaṃ vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntasya hetuvyatirekasya ca vikalpād eva pratipattiḥ.4 /
body.translated_text: And the second [objection] is also irrelevant, because negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is cognized through conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpajñāna</s>). For absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is not some embodied thing that must be directly perceived; rather, it is to be dealt with through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. For it is not the case that absence has no cognition at all other than through conceptual construction, or that it is entirely uncognized — for either way, there would be the unwanted consequence of abandoning its practical usage. Likewise, the cognition of the dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) and of the negative concomitance of the reason is through conceptual construction alone.

body.text: (85.9) tṛtīyam api dūṣaṇam asaṅgatam / vyāpakānupalambhena nirdoṣeṇa sattvasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāpter avyāhatatvāt /
body.translated_text: The third objection too is irrelevant, because the pervasion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) with momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) is uncontradicted, through the faultless non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>).

body.text: (85.11) tad ayaṃ vyāpakānupalambho 'kṣaṇikasyāsattvam / sattvasya tato vyatirekaṃ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiṃ ca sādhayatyekavyāpārātmakatvād iti sthitam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that this non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) establishes the non-existence of the non-momentary, the negative concomitance of existence from that [non-momentary], and the pervasion [of existence] with momentariness — because it has a single operation [accomplishing all three].

body.text: (85.13) nanu vyāpakānupalabdhir iti yady anupalabdhimātraṃ tadā na tasya sādhyabuddhijanakatvam avastutvāt / na cānyopalabdhir vyāpakānupalabdhir abhidhātuṃ śakyā bhūtalādivad anyasya kasya cid anupalabdher iti cet /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, if 'non-perception of the pervader' is merely non-perception, then it cannot generate the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), because it is a non-entity. And the non-perception of the pervader cannot be called the perception of something else — like [the perception of] bare ground and the like — because the non-perception of some other thing [would also qualify]. — If so [is the objection],

body.text: (85.15) tad asaṅgatam / dharmyupalabdher evānyatrānupalabdhitayā vyavasthāpanāt / yathā hi neha śiṃśapā vṛkṣābhāvād ity atra vṛkṣāpekṣayā kevalapradeśasya dharmiṇa upalabdhir vṛkṣānupalabdhiḥ / śiṃśapāpeksayā ca kevalapradeśasya dharmiṇa upalabdhir eva śiṃśapāyā abhāvopalabdhir iti svabhāvahetuparyavasāyivyāpāro vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tathā nityasya dharmiṇo vikalpabuddhyavasitasya kramikāritvākramikāritvāpekṣayā kevalagrahaṇād eva kramikāritvākramikāritvānupalambhaḥ / arthakriyāpekṣayā ca kevalapratītir evārthakriyāyoga pratītir iti vyāpakānupalambhāntarād asya na kaś cid viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: That is irrelevant, because the perception of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) itself is established as non-perception in relation to something else. Just as in 'there is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the absence of a tree' — the perception of the bare location as property-bearer, in relation to 'tree,' is the non-perception of a tree; and the perception of the bare location as property-bearer, in relation to '<s>śiṃśapā</s>,' is itself the perception of the absence of the <s>śiṃśapā</s>. Thus the non-perception of the pervader terminates in [the operation of] the essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). Similarly, the mere apprehension of the permanent property-bearer — established by conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpabuddhi</s>) — in relation to successive and simultaneous causal activity, is itself the non-perception of successive and simultaneous causal activity. And the mere cognition [of the property-bearer] in relation to causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is itself the cognition of the absence of causal efficacy — thus this [argument] has no difference from any other non-perception of the pervader.

body.text: (85.22) adhyavasāyāpekṣayā ca bāhye 'kṣaṇike vastuni vyāpakābhāvād vyāpyābhāvasiddhivyavahāraḥ / adhyavasāyaś ca samanantarapratyayabalād āyātākāraviśeṣayogād agṛhīte 'pi pravartanaśaktir bodhavyaḥ / īdṛśaś cādhyavasāyo 'smaccitrādvaitasiddhau nirvāhitaḥ / sa cāvisaṃvādī vyavahāraḥ parihartum aśakyaḥ / yad vyāpakaśūnyaṃ tadvyāpyaśūnyam iti / etasyaivārthasyānenāpi krameṇa pratipādanāt / ayaṃ ca nyāyo yathā vastubhūte dharmiṇi tathā 'vastubhūte 'pīti ko viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: And through determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), with respect to the external non-momentary object, the practical usage of establishing the absence of the pervaded from the absence of the pervader [is maintained]. And determination should be understood as the power of engaging [with an object] even when not directly apprehended, arising from the force of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) and the connection with a particular form that has been acquired. Such determination has been established in our proof of <s>Citrādvaita</s> (variegated non-duality). And that non-discordant practical usage (<s>avisaṃvādī vyavahāra</s>) cannot be avoided — [namely,] 'what is devoid of the pervader is devoid of the pervaded.' Because this very meaning is demonstrated through this procedure as well. And what difference does this principle make whether the property-bearer is a real entity or not?

body.text: (85.27) tathā hy ekajñānasaṃsargy atra vikalpya eva / yathā ca hariṇaśirasi tenaikajñānasaṃsargiśṛṅgam upalabdhaṃ / śaśaśirasy api tena sahaikajñānasaṃsargitvasambhāvanayaiva śṛṅgaṃ niṣidhyate, tathā nīlādāv apariniṣṭhitanityānityabhāve kramākramau svadharmiṇā sārdham ekajñānasaṃsargiṇau dṛṣṭau, yadi nitye bhavataḥ nityagrāhijñāne svadharmiṇā nityena sahaiva gṛhyeyātām iti sambhāvanaya ekājñānasaṃsargadvārakam eva pratiṣidhyate / kathaṃ punar etasmin nityajñāne kramākramayor asphuraṇam iti yāvatā kramākramakroḍikṛtam eva nityaṃ vikalpayām iti cet. ata eva bādhakāvatāro viparītāropam antareṇa tasya vaiyarthyāt.
body.translated_text: For here, only what is connected with a single cognition (<s>ekajñānasaṃsargin</s>) is to be conceptualized. Just as a horn is perceived as connected with a single cognition with the head of a deer, and is denied of the head of a hare merely by the possibility of its being connected with a single cognition with that [hare's head] — so too, in the case of blue and the like whose permanent or impermanent nature is not yet settled, successive and simultaneous [causal activities], observed as connected with a single cognition with their own property-bearer — if they were to obtain in the permanent, they would have to be grasped in the very cognition that grasps the permanent together with their own property-bearer qua permanent. By the possibility [of such co-cognition], they are denied through the gateway of single-cognition-connection alone. — [Objection:] But how is there a non-appearance of successive and simultaneous [activity] in this cognition of the permanent, given that we conceptualize the permanent as already including successive and simultaneous [activity]? — [Reply:] For this very reason the sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>) enters — because without the superimposition of the contrary, it would be pointless.

body.text: (86.6) kālāntare 'py ekarūpatayā nityatvam. kramākramau ca kṣaṇadvaye bhinnarūpatayā. tato nityatvasya kramākramikāryaśakteś ca parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇatayā durvāro virodha iti kathaṃ nitye kramākramayor antarbhāvaḥ. anantarbhāvāc ca suddhanityavikalpena dūrīkṛtakramākramasamāropeṇa katham ullekhaḥ. tataś ca pratiyogini nitye 'pi vikalpyamāne ekajñānasaṃsargilakṣaṇaprāpte nityopalabdhir eva nityaviruddhasyānupalabhyamānasya kramākramasyānupalabdhiḥ. tata eva cārthakriyāśakter anupalabdhiḥ. tasmād vyāpakavivekidharmyupalabdhitayā na vyāpakānupalambhāntarād asya viśeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: (86.6) And permanence means identity of form across different times. And succession and simultaneity [mean] difference of form in two moments. Therefore, since permanence and the capacity for successive-and-simultaneous causal efficacy have a character defined by mutual exclusion (<s>parasparaparihārasthiti</s>), the contradiction is unavoidable — so how could succession and simultaneity be subsumed under a permanent [entity]? And since they cannot be subsumed, through the conceptual construction of pure permanence — from which the superimposition of succession and simultaneity has been removed — how could [the permanent] appear [as possessing them]? And thus, even when the counter-correlate — the permanent — is conceptualized, since it fulfills the conditions of being an object of a single cognition, the perception of the permanent is itself the non-perception of succession and simultaneity, which are contradictory to the permanent and are not being perceived. And from that itself follows the non-perception of the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>). Therefore, since this [argument] has the character of a perception of a property that distinguishes the pervader (<s>vyāpakavivekin</s>), it is not different from another [form of] non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>).

body.text: (86.13) nanv etad avastudharmikopayogi vastv adhiṣṭhānatvāt pramāṇavyavasthāyā iti cet. kim idaṃ vastvadhiṣṭhānatvam nāma. kiṃ paramparayāpi vastunaḥ sakāśād āgatatvam, atha vastuni kena cid ākāreṇa vyavahārakāraṇatvam, vastubhūtadharmipratibaddhatvaṃ vā.
body.translated_text: (86.13) [Objection:] But this is useful [only] when the property-bearer is a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>), because the system of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) has real entities (<s>vastu</s>) as its basis. — [Reply:] What is meant by this 'having real entities as its basis'? Does it mean (1) having ultimately originated from a real entity, even indirectly? Or (2) being a cause of practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) in some respect regarding a real entity? Or (3) being connected with a property-bearer that is a real entity?

body.text: (86.16) yady ādyaḥ pakṣas tadā kramākramasyārthakriyāyāś ca vyāptigrahaṇagocaravastupratibaddhatvam asyāpi. na kṣīṇam.
body.translated_text: (86.16) If the first alternative, then this [argument] too is connected with a real entity that is within the scope of the apprehension of the pervasion of succession and simultaneity with causal efficacy. It is not exhausted.

body.text: (86.18) na dvitīye 'pi pakṣe dosah sambhavati. kṣaṇabhaṅgivastu sādhanopāyatvād asya.
body.translated_text: (86.18) Nor is there any defect in the second alternative — since this [argument] serves as a means of proving [the existence of] a momentary real entity.

body.text: (86.19) na cāntimo 'pi vikalpaḥ kalpyate. tasyaiva nityavikalpasya vastuno dharmibhūtasya kramākramavad bāhyanityopādānaśūnyatvenārthakriyāvad bāhyanityopādānaśūnyatve prasādhanāt. paryudāsavṛttyā buddhisvabhāvabhūtākṣaṇikākāre vastubhūte dharmiṇi pratibaddhatvasambhavāt.
body.translated_text: (86.19) Nor should the last alternative be posited. For the very conceptual construction of the permanent, [even though] devoid of an external permanent substratum — like succession and simultaneity — is to be proved as [also] devoid of an external permanent substratum, like causal efficacy. [This is possible] because of the possibility of being connected with a property-bearer that is a real entity of the character of a non-momentary aspect (<s>akṣaṇikākāra</s>) that is of the nature of cognition (<s>buddhisvabhāva</s>), [understood] through the method of exclusion (<s>paryudāsavṛtti</s>).

body.text: (86.23) ayam eva nyāyo na vaktā vandhyāsutaś caitanyābhāvād ityādau yojyaḥ. etena yathā vṛkṣābhāvādir antarbhāvayituṃ śakyate na tathāyam iti trilocano 'pi nirastaḥ.
body.translated_text: (86.23) This very same principle should be applied to [arguments such as] 'the speaker is not a barren woman's son, because of the absence of consciousness,' and the like. By this, <s>Trilocana</s>'s [objection] too — that 'this [argument] cannot be subsumed in the same way as the absence of trees and the like [can be subsumed]' — is also refuted.

body.text: (86.25) na ca kramādyabhāvas trayīṃ doṣajātiṃ nātikrāmati, abhāvadharmatve 'pi āśrayāsiddhidoṣaparihārāt.
body.translated_text: (86.25) Nor does the absence of succession and the like fail to escape the threefold class of defects — because even when it has the property of absence (<s>abhāvadharmatva</s>), the defect of unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) is avoided.

body.text: (86.26) yat tvanena pramāṇāntarān nityānām asattvasiddhau kramādivirahasyābhāvadharmatā sidhyatīty uktam, tadvālasyāpi durabhidhānam. nityo hi dharmi. asattvaṃ sādhyam. kramikāryakāritvākramikāryakāritvaviraho hetuḥ. asya cābhāvadharmatvaṃ nāma asattvalakṣaṇasvasādhyāvinābhāvitvam ucyate. tac ca kramākrameṇa sattvasya vyāptisiddhau sattvasya vyāpyasyābhāvena kramākramasya vyāpakasya viraho vyāptaḥ sidhyatīty abhāvadharmatvaṃ prāg eva vidhyor vyāptisādhanāt pratyakṣād anumānād ekasmād vā pramāṇāntarāt siddham iti netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: (86.26) As for what was said by him — that 'the absence-property-nature of the absence of succession and the like is established [only] when the non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) of permanent entities is established by another <s>pramāṇa</s>' — even a child would find that hard to say. For the permanent is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) is the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved); the absence of the capacity for producing effects successively and simultaneously is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). And its 'absence-property-nature' means being invariably concomitant with non-existence, which is its own <s>sādhya</s>. And that [concomitance] is established when the pervasion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) by succession and simultaneity is established — [for then] the absence of succession and simultaneity as the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is pervaded by the absence of existence (<s>sattva</s>) as the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>). Thus, the absence-property-nature is already established — even before the pervasion of the two positive [terms] is established — through perception, inference, or even a single other <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, there is no defect of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>).

body.text: (87.7) na ca sattāyām ivāsattāyām api tulyaḥ prasaṅgo bhinnanyāyatvāt. vastubhūtaṃ hi tatra sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca. tayor dharmy api vastv eva yujyate.
body.translated_text: (87.7) Nor is there an equal absurd consequence in [proving] non-existence as there is in [proving] existence — because the reasoning is different. For in the latter case, both the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) are real entities. And for those, the property-bearer too should properly be a real entity alone.

body.text: (87.9) vastunas tu pratyakṣānumānābhyām eva siddhiḥ. tayor abhāve niyamenāśrayāsiddhir iti yuktam. asattāsādhane tv avastudharmo hetur avastu vikalpamātrasiddhe dharmiṇi nāśrayāsiddhidoṣeṇa dūṣayituṃ śakyaḥ. tathā 'kṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhaḥ sidhyaty eva.
body.translated_text: (87.9) But the establishment of real entities is through perception and inference alone. In their absence, the defect of unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) necessarily follows — and that is justified. But when non-existence (<s>asattā</s>) is being proved, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is a non-real property (<s>avastudharma</s>), and it cannot be vitiated by the defect of unestablished locus in a property-bearer that is a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>) established by mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpamātra</s>). Likewise, the contradiction of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) with succession and simultaneity for a non-momentary entity is indeed established.

body.text: (87.13) tathā vikalpādevākṣaṇiko virodhī siddhaḥ. vikalpollikhitaś cāsya svabhāvo nāpara ity api vyavahartavyam. anyathā tadanuvādena kramākramādirahitatvādiniṣedhādikam uktam. tatsvarūpasyānullekhād anyasyollekhād ity akṣaṇikaśaśaviṣāṇādiśabdānuccāraṇaprasaṅgaḥ. asti ca. ato yathā pramāṇābhāve 'pi vikalpasiddhasya vandhyāsutādeḥ saundaryādiniṣedho 'nurūpas tathā vikalpopanītasyaivākṣaṇikarūpasya tad eva pratyanīkākāreṇa saha virodhavyavasthāyāṃ kīdṛso doṣaḥ syāt. yadi cākṣaṇikānubhavābhāvāt virodhapratiṣedhas tarhi vandhyāputrādyanubhavād eva saundaryādiniṣedho 'pi mābhūt.
body.translated_text: (87.13) Thus, the non-momentary contradictory is established through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. And it should be stated that the nature outlined by conceptual construction is [that entity's nature] and no other. Otherwise, by restating [the opponent's position], the negation of the absence of succession and simultaneity etc. was stated [only about that conceptual entity]. Since the nature of that [non-momentary entity] is not outlined [in reality] and something else is outlined—there would be the absurd consequence of not even being able to utter words like "non-momentary," "hare's horn," etc. But such words are uttered. Therefore, just as the negation of beauty and the like is appropriate for the son of a barren woman etc. established through conceptual construction, even in the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [establishing their real existence], so too when the non-momentary form presented by conceptual construction alone is placed in opposition with that very contradictory aspect—what fault could there be? If the contradiction is denied because of the absence of experience of the non-momentary, then the negation of beauty etc. should also not hold, simply because of the absence of experience of the barren woman's son etc.

body.text: (87.20) nanv evaṃ virodhasyāpāramārthikatvam. taddvāreṇa kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir apy apāramārthikī syād iti cet.
body.translated_text: (87.20) [Objection:] In this case, the contradiction would be non-ultimate (<s>apāramārthika</s>). And through that, the proof of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) too would be non-ultimate.

body.text: (87.21) na hi virodho nāma vastvantaraṃ kiñcit ubhayakoṭidattapādasambandhābhidhānam iṣyate, 'smābhir upapadyate vā. yenaikasambandhino vastutvābhāve 'pāramārthikaṃ syāt. yathā tv iṣyate tathā pāramārthika eva / viruddhābhimatayor anyo 'nyasvarūpaparihāramātraṃ virodhārthaḥ / sa ca bhāvābhāvayoḥ pāramārthika eva / na bhāvo 'bhāvarūpam āviśati / nāpy abhāvo bhāvarūpaṃ praviśatīti yo 'yam anayor asaṃkaraniyamaḥ sa eva pāramārthiko virodhaḥ / kālāntaraikarūpatayā hi nityatvam / kramākramau kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhinnarūpatayā / tato nityatvakramākramikāryakāritvayor bhāvābhāvavad virodho 'sty eva /
body.translated_text: (87.21) [Reply:] No, for contradiction (<s>virodha</s>) is not accepted by us as some other entity (<s>vastvantara</s>), a connection with both terms, nor is it [so] explained. Were it [such an entity], then in the absence of entity-status of one of the relata, it would be non-ultimate. But as it is accepted [by us], it is indeed ultimate. The meaning of contradiction is merely the mutual exclusion of each other's nature (<s>anyonyasvarūpaparihāramātra</s>) of the two considered contradictory. And that [mutual exclusion] between existence (<s>bhāva</s>) and non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) is indeed ultimate. Existence does not enter the form of non-existence, nor does non-existence enter the form of existence. This rule of non-confusion (<s>asaṃkaraniyama</s>) between the two is the ultimate contradiction. For permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is identity of form across different times. Succession and simultaneity involve different forms even in two moments. Therefore, between permanence and successive-and-simultaneous efficient causal action, there is contradiction, just as between existence and non-existence.

body.text: (88.1) nanu nityatvaṃ kramayaugapadyavattvaṃ ca viruddhau dharmau vidhūya nāparo virodho nāma, kasya vāstavatvam iti cet /
body.translated_text: (88.1) [Objection:] Having set aside the two contradictory properties—permanence and the possession of successive and simultaneous [activity]—there is no other [thing called] "contradiction." Whose reality is [this]?

body.text: (88.2) na, na hi dharmāntarasya sambhavena virodhasya pāramārthikatvaṃ brūmaḥ / kiṃ tu viruddhayor dharmayoḥ sadbhāve / anyathā virodhanāmadharmāntarasambhave 'pi yadi na viruddhau dharmau kva pāramārthikavirodhasambhavaḥ / viruddhau ced dharmau tāvataiva tāttviko virodhavyavahāraḥ / kim apareṇa pratijñāmātrasiddhena virodhanāmnā vastvantareṇa /
body.translated_text: (88.2) [Reply:] No, for we do not assert the ultimacy (<s>pāramārthikatva</s>) of the contradiction on the basis of the existence of some other property. Rather, [it rests] on the existence of the two contradictory properties. Otherwise, even if some other entity named "contradiction" existed, if the two properties are not contradictory, where would the possibility of ultimate contradiction be? But if the two properties are contradictory, that alone suffices for the true convention of contradiction. What use is another entity called "contradiction," established by mere assertion?

body.text: (88.7) tad ayaṃ pūrvapakṣasaṃkṣepaḥ / nityaṃ nāsti na vā pratītiviṣayas tenāśrayāsiddhatā hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatir ataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca / śūnyaś ca dvitayena sidhyati na vā 'sattā 'pi sattā yathā no nityena virodhasiddhir asatā śakyā kramāder api / iti /
body.translated_text: (88.7) So this is the summary of the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>): [Verse:] The permanent either does not exist or is not an object of cognition; hence the locus of the reason is unestablished, and one's own experience is damaged; the positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) too is thereby rejected. The void is not established by both [means]; non-existence is not [established] like existence. Nor is the establishment of contradiction possible with the permanent—incapable even of succession and the like.

body.text: (88.12) atra siddhāntasaṃkṣepaḥ / dharmasya kasya cid avastuni mānasiddhā bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kim ihāsti no vā / kvāpy asti cet katham iyanti na dūṣaṇāni nāsty eva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: (88.12) Here is the summary of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>): [Verse:] Is there, or is there not, the convention of sublation (<s>bādhā</s>) and establishment (<s>vidhi</s>)—validated by a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)—with regard to any property of a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>)? If it exists somewhere, then how [can you avoid] these many faults? If it does not exist at all, then the consequence of contradicting one's own statement is established.

body.text: (88.17) tad vam nityaṃ na kramikāryakāritvākramikāryakāritvayogīti paramārthaḥ / tataś ca sattāyuktam api naiveti paramārthaḥ / tataś ca kṣaṇikākṣaṇikaparihāreṇa rāśyantarābhāvād akṣaṇikān nivartamānam idaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇika eva viśrāmyatvena vyāptaṃ sidhyatīti sattvāt kṣaṇikatvasiddhir avirodhini /
body.translated_text: (88.17) Thus, the ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>) is that the permanent is not endowed with either successive or simultaneous efficient causal action. And therefore, the ultimate meaning is that it is not endowed with existence (<s>sattā</s>) either. And therefore, since there is no other class besides the momentary and the non-momentary, this existence (<s>sattva</s>)—withdrawing from the non-momentary—rests in the momentary alone, and is thus pervaded [by momentariness], and is established. Hence the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) from existence is non-contradictory.

body.text: (88.21) prakṛtiḥ sarvadharmāṇaṃ yad bodhān muktir iṣyate / sa eva tīrthyanirmāthī kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ prasāditaḥ /
body.translated_text: (88.21) [Verse:] That very momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>)—since the nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all phenomena (<s>dharma</s>) is such that liberation (<s>mukti</s>) is attained through its realization (<s>bodha</s>)—the confuter of the heterodox (<s>tīrthya</s>), has been elucidated.

body.text: (88.23) iti kṛtir iyaṃ ratnakīrteḥ /
body.translated_text: (88.23) This is the composition of <s>Ratnakīrti</s>.
